podcast.body: Recorded in Los Angeles with producer Dave Jordan, Show Me came out at the very beginning of what is now called the Can Rock Renaissance. The band wanted to return to the sound of the Green Album, but the record label pushed for a bigger production influenced by the rising sound of U2. Singles included "One Day in Your Life" and "One Gun." Neil Osborne later called it his least favorite 54-40 record, describing it as overproduced. A bridge for "One Day in Your Life" — unusual for a band that "didn't even know what bridges were" — was literally cut into a tape and physically spliced in by producer Jordan when he flew up from Los Angeles to Toronto during a show at the Diamond. "That was our first sort of compromise that I felt we made against our instinct."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album was considered a "learning experience" for the band, as they followed the "path of least resistance" with producers and record company people they knew. It is the only record that one band member states they "can't even listen to anymore." "That's the only record that we made that I can't even listen to anymore."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
